title: Essentially constant inverse system of abelian groups (Stacks 05PU (2))
statement: Let $(B_i)_{i\ge1}$ be an inverse system of abelian groups [def-weil-inverse-system], with composite transition homomorphisms $B_k\to B_i$ for $k\ge i$. The system is *essentially constant* (with *value* $X$) if there are an abelian group $X$ with homomorphisms $\pi_i:X\to B_i$ compatible with the transition maps ($B_{i+1}\to B_i$ composed with $\pi_{i+1}$ is $\pi_i$), an index $i_0\ge1$ and a homomorphism $r:B_{i_0}\to X$ such that (a) $r\circ\pi_{i_0}=\mathrm{id}_X$, and (b) for every $j\ge1$ there is $k\ge\max(i_0,j)$ such that the transition map $B_k\to B_j$ equals the composite $\pi_j\circ r\circ(B_k\to B_{i_0})$.

split_report.summary: Read Categories 05PU (2) and 05PV (categories.tex 2911--2980) and the two citers' sources (Homology 070C, 070D, 070E, homology.tex 7733--7866). The statement is kept unchanged: for the index category (Z_{>=1}, >=) the morphisms k -> i_0 and k -> j of 05PU (2)(b) exist (uniquely) iff k >= max(i_0, j), the cone condition of 05PU is compatibility with the maps B_{i+1} -> B_i (equivalent to compatibility with all composites B_k -> B_i, by def-weil-inverse-system), and (a), (b) are 05PU (2)(a), (b) with M_k -> M_i -> X -> M_j written pi_j o r o (B_k -> B_{i_0}); 05PV only says an inverse system is essentially constant when its diagram over I^opp is. Both citers use exactly this notion as a hypothesis (070E inline text agrees word for word; 070D uses it through 070C, whose proof uses the same factorisation for j >= i). The statement is self-contained; its only notion besides abelian groups and homomorphisms is the inverse system with its composite transition maps, which def-weil-inverse-system defines (stmt_deps kept). Source place extended by 05PV. Mathlib: no counterpart; the nearest, IsCofiltered.IsEventuallyConstant / Functor.IsEventuallyConstantTo (Limits/Constructions/EventuallyConstant.lean:278, :38), is strictly stronger (counterexample in the grep search entry), so no mathlib_match or mathlib_candidate.
